audit_notes: Model: tensioned membrane on an elastic (Winkler) foundation spanning one lattice cell between rigid septa, T w'' - k w = -p, normalized by cell size L; lambda^2 = k L^2/T = 5e7*4e-6/50 = 4. Analytical: w(x) = (p/k)[1 - cosh(lambda(x-1/2))/cosh(lambda/2)], mean deflection = (p/k)(1 - tanh(lambda/2)/(lambda/2)) = 0.238 p/k = 2.1e-7 m for p = 45 Pa; mean compliance C = 4.8e-9 m/Pa. Fouling release via Kendall: sigma_c = sqrt(2 w_a/C) = sqrt(0.16/4.8e-9) = 5.8 kPa. Baseline: standard silicone foul-release layer (G = 0.33 MPa, t = 0.3 mm -> k = G/t = 1.1e9 Pa/m) without lattice, represented by a very large cell (cell_size = 0.05 m, so the clamping edges do not matter: mean deflection 0.99 p/k), silicone surface w_a = 0.05: C = 9.0e-10, sigma_c = 10.5 kPa -> expected ~45% lower release stress. CAVEATS: (1) the mean-deflection compliance mixes very compliant cell centres with rigid septa lines; barnacles (5-15 mm) span several cells and the septa lines carry stress concentrations, so the real release benefit is smaller; (2) the 'foundation stiffness' of gel-filled cells is taken as G_gel/h and ignores gel incompressibility (a confined, incompressible gel is much stiffer in the normal direction unless cells are vented/foamed) - this is the largest uncertainty; (3) no drag quantity is computed; cell natural frequency f = (1/2L) sqrt(T/m') with m' ~ 1 kg/m2 including added mass -> ~1.8 kHz, mistuned from the ~300 Hz burst band, so drag effect ~0. Stability: membrane dimple depth 0.2 um under p' is hydraulically smooth (k+ ~ 0.03); static divergence unlikely with T = 50 N/m. Durability: tough skin is an improvement; septa-membrane bond fatigue and water ingress through cuts are risks. Dimensionless: lambda^2 = 4, dimple k+ = 0.03, f_cell/f_burst ~ 6.
